symbols.name: first kernel scalar
symbols.meaning: The first scalar of a two-point kernel $\alpha I+\beta X$, the coefficient of the identity term.
symbols.quote: Each kernel is $\alpha I+\beta X$, where $\alpha$ is the first scalar of the kernel and $\beta$ is the second scalar.

symbols.name: second kernel scalar
symbols.meaning: The second scalar of a two-point kernel $\alpha I+\beta X$, the coefficient of the swap term.
symbols.quote: Each kernel is $\alpha I+\beta X$, where $\alpha$ is the first scalar of the kernel and $\beta$ is the second scalar.

symbols.name: identity on two points
symbols.meaning: The identity map on a pair of points, which leaves both coordinates unchanged.
symbols.quote: Each frame change is a product of two-point kernels, where $I$ is the identity on two points and $X$ is the map that swaps them.

symbols.name: swap on two points
symbols.meaning: The map on a pair of points that exchanges its two coordinates.
symbols.quote: Each frame change is a product of two-point kernels, where $I$ is the identity on two points and $X$ is the map that swaps them.

relations.quote: A complex phase network is built on a [Subset-intersection network](subset-intersection-network.md) with a frame change on each edge.
Each frame change takes its scalars from [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md), so every sum and product stays exact, with no rounding.
Each wire is labelled by [Subspace labels](subspace-labels.md).
Applied to all selected address bits at once, the network is a [Tensor product](tensor-product.md) of one kernel per bit, evaluated on all addresses.
